correctness.rationale: On a countably infinite indiscrete space every point's only neighbourhood is N; consequently the omega-accumulation diamond of a subset is N iff the set is infinite and empty iff finite, while box is the cofinite test. Modal normality follows from cofinite filter closure; D, 4 and 5 follow by direct set tests. For any KD45 countermodel, choose a root r in a serial transitive Euclidean frame and S=R(r). Euclideanness and transitivity prove every u in S has R(u)=S. A counterformula uses finitely many atoms, so partition N into a finite family of infinite blocks indexed by the realized S atom-types, and if r∉S reserve a singleton with r's atoms. Induction on subformulas identifies truth on each block with its type in S and at the selected singleton/root; the diamond test is existence of an infinite satisfying block and box is all S-types satisfying (finite exceptional singleton is harmless). Thus every KD45-invalid formula fails in the fixed space. Non-Kripke representability also follows immediately since the operator fails arbitrary-union preservation: each singleton maps to empty but their union N maps to N. No finite-model shortcut or T1 hypothesis is used.

evidence: A K4 theorem over the entire class allows more countermodels and does not determine the stronger logic of one fixed member. The T1 collapse does not apply to indiscrete N.
